title: REPORT on EU-Syria political relations
part_text: 48. Expresses concern over the safety of Syria’s Christian communities, including Syriac Orthodox, Greek Orthodox, Armenian Apostolic, Armenian Catholic, Armenian Evangelical, Chaldean Catholic, Apostolic Catholic Assyrian, Maronite, Latin Catholic, Syriac Catholic, Melkite Greek Catholic, Baptist, Anglican Episcopal, Presbyterian, Evangelical and Pentecostal communities, which continue to be exposed to documented intimidation and violence from multiple actors; strongly condemns the brutal terrorist attack of 22 June 2025 against the Greek Orthodox Mar Elias Church in Damascus, which claimed 25 lives and injured over 60 people, leaving Christians across Syria deeply shaken and afraid; also condemns the attacks in Suqaylabiyah, as well as the brutal attack on the Melkite Greek Catholic Archbishop of the Diocese of Homs, Hama, Nabk and Yabroud on 14 November 2026 in his church in Homs, which was looted; demands that the Syrian transitional authorities take the necessary steps to ensure the safety and protection of Syria’s Christian communities; recognises the climate of fear and uncertainty in which Christians in Syria have been forced to live for decades; underlines the fundamental importance of preserving and cherishing the historical contributions of Christian and other communities to Syria’s rich religious and cultural heritage, including through the protection of churches, monasteries, cemeteries, religious heritage sites and clergy; calls for Syria’s emerging political architecture to be fully reflective of this diversity, and for the equal participation of these communities in political, constitutional and administrative reconstruction efforts to be ensured;
